{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=cognitive+architecture+models+for+long-term+preference+formation+versus+transient+behavior&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7126885\", \"title\": [\"Preference Heterogeneity versus Economic Incentives:What Determines Long-Term Care Arrangements in Europe?\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Care arrangements vary widely across families and countries. To understand why, wedevelop a tractable static bargaining model of family long-term-care choices and estimateit using European data. Families choose among child-provided informal care,including which child becomes the caregiver, formal home care, mixed care, and nursing-homecare, taking into account both monetary costs and heterogeneous non-monetarypreferences over care arrangements. Preference heterogeneity strongly dampens policyresponsiveness: without it, a 20% subsidy to nursing-home and formal-home-care costsraises the use of formal care by 7.5%, compared with only 4.0% in the baseline model.Cross-country differences in care arrangements are shaped more by non-monetary factorsthan by formal-care prices. Looking ahead, the model predicts a substantial increasein demand for formal care by 2050, driven by a declining ratio of adult children toelderly parents, with the largest increases in countries where informal care is currentlypredominant.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7126885\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5204/thesis.eprints.268426\", \"title\": [\"Long-Term Generative Models for Multimodal Behavior in Soccer\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This thesis develops deep learning algorithms for modelling long-term behaviours in soccer, spanning both continuous player and ball motion and the discrete actions that structure a match. These models address two long-standing industry-level challenges: collecting complete trajectories across all televised games, and labelling actions in those games in a semi-automated manner. The methods developed in this thesis have been deployed commercially, substantially increasing the scale and efficiency of soccer data collection.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5204/thesis.eprints.268426\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.21511/imfi.18(2).2021.18\…

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=symmetry+breaking+in+multi-agent+reinforcement+learning+environments+path+dependence&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1109/dac63849.2025.11132657\", \"title\": [\"Late Breaking Results: Breaking Symmetry— Unconventional Placement of Analog Circuits using Multi-Level Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/dac63849.2025.11132657\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2025, 6, 22]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.65148/ecn/2025017\", \"title\": [\"Optimal Path Planning of Swarm Robots Using Multi Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning in Dynamic Environments\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The problem of optimal path planning among swarm robots under dynamic conditions is a critical problem since obstacles cannot be predicted, inter-robots can collide and coordinated navigation is required. The traditional approaches to path planning, including A-, D-, potential field-, rapidly exploring random trees (RRT), and particle swarm optimization (PSO), are not always effective in the multi-agent dynamic environment, which results in inefficiency of trajectories and the higher probability of collisions. To overcome these difficulties, this paper suggests a Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Swarm Path Planning (MADRL-SPP) framework, which would allow the swarm robots to navigate in an adaptive way, with zero collisions, and consuming minimal energy. The suggested MADRL-SPP framework describes every robot as an intelligent agent that interacts with the environment and other agents and benefits collective trajectories using the method of reward-based learning. The simulations that are undertaken using MATLAB are performed within dynamic operating environments, where obstacles are moving, the speed of the robots is heterogeneous and there are communication constraints. Performance analysis takes into account efficiency of the paths, the collision rate, convergence rate, the energy use and the scalability. Comparative analysis shows that MADRL-SPP is greatly superior to the traditional methods, such as A-, D-, potential field, RRT-, and PSO by being up to 32 percent more efficient in path, 45 percent less colliding, and converges quicker in dynamic conditions. {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=sunk+cost+fallacy+in+scientific+research+management+and+agenda+abandonment&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.3202990\", \"title\": [\"The Sunk Cost ‘Fallacy’ Is Not a Fallacy\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Business and Economic textbooks warn against committing the Sunk Cost Fallacy: you, rationally, shouldn't let unrecoverable costs influence your current decisions. In this paper, I argue that this isn't, in general, correct. Sometimes it's perfectly reasonable to wish to carry on with a project because of the resources you've already sunk into it. The reason? Given that we're social creatures, it's not unreasonable to care about wanting to act in such a way so that a plausible story can be told about you according to which your diachronic behavior doesn't reveal that you've suffered, what I will call, diachronic misfortune. Acting so as to hide that you've suffered diachronic misfortune involves striving to make yourself easily understood while disguising any shortcomings that might damage your reputation as a desirable teammate. And making yourself easily understood to others while hiding your flaws will, sometimes, put pressure on you to honor sunk costs.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3202990\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2018]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.33915/etd.3486\", \"title\": [\"Age, Expertise, and the Sunk-Cost Fallacy\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.33915/etd.3486\"}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.3350804\", \"title\": [\"Transferable Sunk Cost Hypothesis: A New Analysis of Sunk Cost Fallacy\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3350804\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2019]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.21955/mep.1115651.1\", \"title\": [\"The sunk cost fallacy in medical education\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.21955/mep.1115651.1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 10, 14]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "6128d1fdbbc0f7430cadc5629e188130492cde18f5e1c6646517f0b9071c2d6c", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "question_abandonment", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.3202990", "doi:10.33915/etd.3486", "doi:10.…
